review_style.value: Spot-checks, no line-by-line: crapper, dryer and mutator gate the code, other agents review, then a human look at structure and behaviour
review_style.quote: With reasonable constraints, like crapper, dryer, and mutator, agents can do a good enough job to allow a responsible engineer to spot-check the code rather than do line-by-line reviews.

also.quote: I want the overall gestalt, not a detailed line-by-line understanding.
I'm using codex to review the code that grok wrote.  Good results.
A simple demo of uml-viewer.  This is how I review the projects I create with agents nowadays.

My current strategy is to not read any of the code written by my agents. That’s the only way I can take advantage of their productivity. What I do instead is to surround the agents with extreme constraints.
People seem shocked that the author of Clean Code doesn't read code anymore.
In order to manage them properly we must know the principles that guide their work, and we must spot check their work to make sure that they are following those principles.
Humans are slow at code.  Agents are fast.  So reading code is a liability.
I use many tools to scrutinize the output of the agents. I just don’t put my eyes directly on the code.
I'll have codex review grok's code, for example.  I also sometimes do spot checks depending on what behaviors I observe.
Each of these requires significant interrogation and review of verification procedures; but not review of the code.
